results.name: First Light Focus Fund
results.management_company_description:
First Light Asset Management is an investment firm focused on identifying health care companies it believes provide high investment potential for clients. Its 14 team members, including six senior investment professionals, invest primarily in micro- to mid-cap stocks across a diversified set of health care subsectors — biotech, medical devices and equipment, diagnostic tools, health care information technology, health care services, and specialty pharmaceuticals. 
First Light believes the following are key to their approach to health care investing:
• History of finding innovative and disruptive companies that change the way health care is practiced
• A consistent process that drives us to companies that are delivering better care at a lower price
• Limited-capacity investment vehicles, allowing for high concentration in the firm’s best ideas, even though they are often micro- to small-cap stocks
• Capitalizing on greater pricing inefficiency among smaller companies
• Diversification to take advantage of low correlation between subsectors
• Probability-weighted analysis to form firm’s view of a stock’s intrinsic value, which determines long or short position and sizing
results.strategy_description: The First Light Focus Fund (the “Fund”) is a concentrated, long-biased small- to micro-cap limited partnership seeking to invest in innovative and disruptive companies within the large and growing health care sector. The Fund aims to achieve a high level of capital appreciation and opportunistically looks to short for alpha creation, while minimizing undue risk to the portfolio. First Light Asset Management, LLC (“First Light”) primarily pursues this investment objective through longer-term investments in publicly traded equity securities it believes will create value over a 2 to 5+ year time horizon. The firm diversifies the portfolio among what it believes are “best-of-breed” health care companies operating in various health care subsectors, including medical devices and equipment, diagnostic tools, health care information technology, biotech, health care services, and specialty pharmaceuticals. First Light believes the inefficient pricing of securities within the small- to micro-cap range, combined with the growth in health care spending, is creating opportunities the investment team can capitalize on through its proprietary investment process. In First Light’s view, small companies are, in certain instances, better positioned to react to the changing health care landscape as they can often more quickly respond to changing market dynamics and provide innovative solutions to address market needs — such as reducing the cost of care and improving patient outcomes.

results.strategy_description:
In January 2018 we launched our Merger Arbitrage strategy, which is currently available in Luxembourg RAIF format with monthly liquidity. We aim to launch the daily liquidity - Article 8 SFDR - UCITS vehicle, in partnership with Alma Capital. The UCITS Fund will be run (as much as possible) pari passu with the Luxembourg RAIF.

The main characteristics of the strategy are the following:

- aims to achieve uncorrelated returns with low volatility compared to equity markets 

- can invest globally with a focus on Europe (~70%)

- investments are made in announced M&A deals (~70-80%), as well as pre and post M&A situations

- investments are made across the entire capital structure (~30% credit)

- strives to have a short to medium duration and focuses on mid/large cap companies 

- fundamental approach is at the basis of all investments

- ESG integrated into the investment process 

- limited leverage, typically below 2.5x

- portfolio manager has 15+ years’ experience running merger arb strategies

results.strategy_description:
Starboard's Established Investment Strategy: Value, Plan, Path:

• 'Value' is a determination based on hard asset values and/or highly discounted cash flows (not relative value multiples).
• 'Plan' is the identification of companies with (i) a good core business generating substantial earnings and cash flow and (ii) a failing growth initiative losing money and negatively impacting consolidated results. In order to refocus on the good core business, these failing growth initiatives should be exited, potentially resulting in significant improvements in consolidated earnings and cash flow.
• 'Path' relates to Starboard's ability to mount an election contest, if necessary, with the goal of making changes to the board of directors to seek to ensure that the 'Plan' to create value is implemented.

Starboard's Investment Opportunities:

• Focus on situations where there is an opportunity to drive operational change
• Seek to have a consistent and formulaic approach to measuring position and portfolio risk
• Typical portfolio of 20 - 35 investments divided between "lead" and "seed" positions
• Aims to practice a disciplined methodology around position sizing and portfolio hedging

results.name: Lykos Global Master Fund LP
results.management_company_description: Lykos Global Management is a newly launched Event-Driven investment firm focused on Equity Capital Markets. Lykos was founded by Nick Laster, the youngest ever Partner at Soros Fund Management (“SFM”). Nick worked at SFM for nearly a decade as Global Head of Equity Capital Markets and Late-Stage Privates. Lykos believe they have developed an “All-Weather”, idiosyncratic strategy that can generate uncorrelated, positive returns in any market environment. They feel their approach preserves the appeal of traditional Event-Driven mandates (i.e., short duration trades, clearly defined catalysts), while also enabling greater capital efficiency and a less cyclical return profile than conventional strategies.  Lykos went live with two sizable anchors in March, 2024 and have generated performance despite muted activity in capital markets. With a historic backlog of companies needing to tap public markets, they believe the set-up for 2025 and beyond is highly compelling.
results.strategy_description: The Fund seeks to compound capital at attractive risk adjusted returns through the market cycle by investing in high quality, competitively advantaged businesses undergoing event driven dislocations.  The three distinct but complementary sub-strategies are Late Stage Privates (LTSP), Core Equity Capital Markets (ECM) and Tactical Opportunities (TacOpps). The LTSP piece focuses on high quality pre-IPO privates (companies going public within twelve months) that comprise up to twenty five percent of the portfolio. The ECM piece seeks to establish positions in exceptional businesses through IPOs and other equity issuance while the TacOpps seeks to capitalize on idiosyncratic, liquidity-driven events in newly public companies.

results.management_company_description: Bengal Asset Management, LLC, a U.S. SEC registered investment advisor, was formed in April 2013 to focus on investment opportunities in Japan. In June 2013 BAM launched its Japan focused equity Long/Short strategy. Driven by a core team of diverse individuals who have been with the firm since inception, the team leverages their extensive collective experience both in Asia and globally to bring a powerful network of relationships, research depth, and broad market expertise across all facets of the business. results.strategy_description:
The Bengal 2 Fund is a Japan focused long-short equity fund. Our investment philosophy combines a core fundamental approach that allows us to express our medium-long term outlook, with a shorter term tactical component that utilizes a broad range of quantitative tools. The balance between the various styles will vary depending on the type of market environment we are facing. Our varied approach to investment makes our strategy more dynamic in nature and allows us to deploy capital in a manner that aims to optimize our focus towards the best opportunities in a highly risk managed fashion. 

The Fund makes public equity investments predominately in Japan through a hedged approach by taking long as well as short positions. Investments are identified through a combination of our fundamental, tactical and quantitative research. The portfolios are built from the bottom-up. They generally do not have significant idea or theme biases but will take advantage of any short-term or long-term trend identified through bottom-up or top-down analysis. At any given time expect the Fund to have 7-15 themes in the portfolio. Investments are made across the market cap structure (from small to mega cap) with the balance of the portfolio primarily dependent on liquidity and the prevailing market environment. Short positions are used to both mitigate against general market risk and to enhance performance.

results.strategy_description:
The fund is dedicated to artificial intelligence and related investments, guided by three core principles:

1/Intelligence technology breakthroughs as the primary investment thesis
2/Intelligence itself representing the largest-scale application
3/Focus on tracking globally leading innovation teams and R&D capabilities

The fund combines fundamental research and a balanced approach to risk.  emphasizing technical expertise, business model innovation, and sustainable long-term returns through multi-strategy portfolio management.

Portfolio Allocation：
Infrastructure Layer (25%): high-performance computing design and manufacturing houses, data centers, cloud infrastructure, and networking equipments
Platform Layer (30-35%): LLM developers, AI training platforms, cloud service providers, enterprise AI solutions, and open-source framework creators
Application Layer (30-40%): Internet platforms, enterprise digitalization solutions, and AI-native applications

Stock selection is based on competitiveness (technology moat, product roadmap and etc), market position (market share, customer retention and etc) and financial metrics (revenue growth, profitability, cash flow) and valuation comparisons.

The fund employs long-short strategies with dynamic position adjustment, derivatives-based hedging, and diversification limits (no single position exceeding 20%). The investment process combines industry research, company assessment and risk-optimized portfolio construction.

Annualized ITD Net Return is a hypothetical rate of return that converts the cumulative ITD return of the fund to an annual rate computed on a time-weighted basis. ITD net returns represent the cumulative returns since inception, compounded monthly.

Firm AUM represents the unaudited estimated net assets under management of LibreMax and Trimaran and includes subscriptions/redemptions as of the date of this document. Trimaran Advisors’ AUM is calculated based upon the principal balance of collateral obligations and cash within the CLOs under management, as well as the principal balance of collateral obligations held in warehouse facilities. For entities within their respective investment periods, LibreMax’s AUM includes committed but uncalled capital.  For entities outside their respective investment periods, LibreMax’s AUM includes the NAV of the Fund and uncalled capital commitments required to pay down any subscription facility utilization or fund future trade commitments.

Annualized ITD Standard Deviation is a measure of the portfolio’s variation of return from its average return since inception. 

Sharpe Ratio is a measure of excess return per unit of risk of the portfolio since the Fund’s inception. It is the annualized value of the excess return over the annualized return of 1 month US Treasury Bills, which is used to represent a risk free rate of return, divided by the portfolio’s Annualized Standard Deviation. 

Max Drawdown represents the largest consecutive percentage decline from peak to trough since the Fund’s inception. Months to Recover represents the number of months from the Fund’s trough to a new high (the recovery).

Correlations measure the relationship between the Onshore Feeder Fund’s performance to the S&P 500 and the Barclays HY Bond Indices since the Onshore Feeder Fund’s inception (10/1/10). The S&P 500 Total Return Index is an unmanaged index of common stock prices of 500 widely held U.S. stocks that include the reinvestment of dividends. The Barclays U.S. High Yield Index provides a measure of performance for USD-denominated, high yield, fixed-rate corporate bond market. Gross Exposure is calculated as total market value of all long credit positions held by the Fund, plus the notional value of credit derivatives where the Fund is selling protection (the “Gross Long Credit Market Value”), divided by the Fund’s estimated net asset value, prior to any adjustments for end of month redemptions or subsequent month subscriptions, (the “Fund NAV”). Cash, cash equivalents and derivatives used for hedging purposes are excluded. 

Net Exposure is calculated as (A) Gross Long Credit Market Value less (B) the sum of the market value of all credit securities held short by the Fund, the market value adjusted notional of any credit derivatives where the Fund is buying protection, and the delta adjusted market value of any options (the “Gross Short Credit Market Value”); divided by the Fund NAV. Cash, cash equivalents and interest rate derivatives are excluded.

IInterest Rate Duration, or effective duration, is a calculation of the interest rate sensitivity of a security to a change in interest rates. Interest Rate Duration is calculated using cash flows based on internal cash flow projections based upon changes in interest rates derived from LibreMax’s proprietary model using base case assumptions, which are available upon request.

Spread Duration, or modified duration, is a metric of price sensitivity calculated as a percentage change in price for a unit change in spread. Bond cash flows are generated from LibreMax's proprietary model using base case assumptions, which are available upon request. Price sensitivity is measured after the discounting spread (over the spot curve) is shocked up and down by 50 basis points.

results.strategy_description:
The flagship Cheyne European Strategic Value Credit (SVC) Fund series invests in predominantly senior secured debt obligations, with a focus on providing constructive capital solutions to mid-market corporates. To maximise flexibility and capitalise on less crowded, underserved segments of the credit market, the funds are capacity constrained, with a strategic emphasis on mid-market opportunities and smaller transaction sizes. The team places emphasis on downside protection and loss avoidance, with entry valuations that correspond more closely with recovery value floors under worst case outcomes.

results.portfolio_additional_details:
The portfolio is broken down into four main components; Stressed Situations, Restructuring, Rescue Financing and Opportunistic.

Stressed Situations: the fund targets secondary purchases of debt at meaningful discounts to fair value, underpinned by comprehensive fundamental analysis. Investment theses are generally predicated on discounted entry prices with a clear path to par and may incorporate covenant relief or other waivers to facilitate operational turnaround.

Restructuring: this approach focuses on acquiring debt at significant discounts to par and intrinsic value, where the thesis is driven by a formal balance sheet restructuring. Transactions typically involve partial debt-to-equity conversions alongside the reinstatement of new debt facilities or revised borrowing terms.

Rescue Financing: the fund originates and provides new money solutions to businesses facing financial or liquidity challenges. These may include stressed refinancing arrangements or liquidity bridge financings, structured as senior or super-senior secured instruments.

Opportunistic: this strategy seeks to exploit periods of elevated market volatility and price dislocation in tradeable debt securities following sector or market shocks.

results.management_company_description: Zentific Investment Management Limited is a Hong Kong-based equity quant boutique. Our quantitative insights aim to emphasize faster Trading Strategies with an intraday to several week time horizon alongside gauges of Local Sentiment. The research process seeks to focus on local and niche data sources with a robust technology infrastructure for natural language processing (NLP) and AI techniques to gather large/unstructured/text data sets.
results.strategy_description:
The Zentific team consists entirely of investment professionals who have been Asian quantitative specialists for the vast majority/entirety of their careers and who bring together what we believe to be deep local knowledge combined with cutting edge data science abilities. The team members are all based locally and work in an integrated PM-research-trading team which we believe allows the group to be more focused and connected to Asia-Pacific's diverse and nuanced markets and drives innovative research ideas.

The Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Master Fund is a systematic market neutral equity long/short hedge fund launched in July of 2015 with two feeder funds: Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Feeder Fund ("Fund") and Zentific Asia Opportunities Offshore Feeder Fund II ("Fund II") sit under the Master Fund. Fund II has a higher risk profile than Fund. The Fund targets meaningful exposure across Asia and has markedly more exposure in EM markets than DM markets. Zentific's research process is focused on local and niche data sources and judicious use is made of NLP and AI techniques (for large/unstructured/text data sets) in all parts of the investment process where it makes sense.

Zentific's investment process uses four main alpha drivers - the Macro Model and three sets of stock selection insights: Fundamentals, Trading Strategies and Local Sentiment. The Macro Model gauges current market conditions versus history and targets more weight to stock selection signals that are expected to work in the coming macro environment. This model is based on a deep set of slow and fast moving country-specific macro-level data sets. Additionally, if the model views the period to offer fewer opportunities, the level of gross exposure will be adjusted.

The strategy's stock selection drivers are grouped into three categories: Trading Strategies - react to flows and events, trading on shorter term mis-pricings, some of which can be implemented intraday or real-time; Local Sentiment - access local data sources (news, portals, blogs) to gain insights on the sentiment of local market participants, often using multi-lingual NLP/deep learning techniques; Fundamentals - focus on the fundamentals of companies and their values in the medium term and uses for example alternative data, industry and country specific insights and accounting insights.

Zentific uses a customised risk model (adjusted to measure many country-specific risk factors) and an in-house transaction cost model, along with the alpha forecasts from the stock selection models, to build the portfolio. Risk management is built into all levels of the investment process, from selective neutralisation of risk factors in the alpha weighting process to both linear and non-linear controls on exposure to common style factors like momentum, value and low risk in the optimisation.

results.strategy_description:
The Suvretta Master Fund, Ltd. (“Suvretta Master Fund” or “Suvretta”) is a long/short equity strategy that began investing on September 1, 2012, and is managed by Aaron Cowen. Suvretta Master Fund’s investment objective is to generate positive absolute returns throughout market cycles by investing primarily in highly liquid, large-capitalization equity securities, both long and short. Suvretta adheres to an “industry before company” investment framework that we believe enables us to construct an “all-weather” portfolio across sectors and market factors.

Suvretta’s core investment strategy is to own good companies in industries that we perceive to have secular growth and on the short side, seek companies in industries that we believe are in secular decline. Utilizing what we believe to be our differentiated “industry before company” investment framework, the team conducts due diligence on both industry and business fundamentals, focusing on competitive strengths and weaknesses, revenue growth, profitability, liquidity, and free cash flow. The investment team develops models for each company in which it may invest to determine earnings potential and underlying intrinsic value. Suvretta typically aims to hold core investments for one to three years, however, positions and position sizes are managed relative to disciplined price-target estimates, subject to changing fundamental theses and economic conditions. The portfolio contains approximately 20 to 40 long positions and 15 to 30 short positions, and the top 10 long positions typically comprise around 60% of the portfolio. On average, gross exposure ranges between 150% and 225% and net exposure ranges between 30% and 60%. The portfolio is primarily focused on companies in North America and Western Europe.

The Suvretta Master Fund portfolio is managed by Aaron Cowen, in collaboration with Director of Research, Corey Metz, and their team of sector-focused analysts. Mr. Cowen has over 28 years of experience as a Portfolio Manager and analyst at Suvretta, Soros, SAC (now Point 72), Karsch and Baupost. Mr. Metz spent 15 years as a Portfolio Manager and Analyst at Point 72 and Caxton Associates, prior to joining Suvretta in 2022.

Investors access the Fund through two feeder funds: (a) SPF Securitized Products Fund Ltd. a Cayman Islands Corporation (Offshore Feeder), and (b) SPF Securitized Products Fund, L.P. a Delaware Limited Partnership (Onshore Feeder).

results.management_company_description:
Unifi Asset Management is a market-neutral relative value asset management firm based in NYC. We primarily invest in USD and EUR-denominated credit derivatives, while taking cross-asset views in corporate credit, cash equities and options. Our discretionary investment process is underpinned by extensive in-house quantitative infrastructure. We leverage in-house technology to preprocess large sets of market data and model the risks and returns of every asset in our investment universe. This enables us to identify mispriced trade pairs across markets, which we opportunistically combine into market-neutral strategy portfolios. The Unifi portfolio is actively managed to have no directional market exposure, limited left-tail drawdown risk and mitigated secondary exposures to convexity, jump to default and other risk factors. 
Unifi was founded by Omer Gundogdu, previously Senior Partner and Portfolio Manager at One William Street. Omer is joined by 4 seasoned Partners with strong relationships and a history of working together. Unifi plans to launch in Q1 of 2025 with launch AUM of over $500mm.
 Unifi's mission is clear: to serve our investors by aiming to provide strong returns and uphold the highest standards of integrity and accountability. Equally important is our commitment to our employees - we recognize our team members are our greatest asset, which is why we are focused on fostering a supportive and collaborative environment. Unifi is dedicated to delivering exceptional value to investors and our employees.
results.strategy_description:
Unifi seeks to generate significant alpha via an actively managed market-neutral portfolio of pair trades in credit derivatives, corporate credit and equities. Using a robust suite of asset pricing models, we identify pricing discrepancies between markets we believe are interconnected (e.g. CDS vs. bond, CDX tranche vs. CDX index, CDS vs. equity) and construct relative value pair trades that stand to benefit from these discrepancies. We combine these pair trades into strategy portfolios that seek to have no directional market risk, limited left-tail drawdown risk and positive exposure to the return drivers that we believe will generate long term outperformance.
 
Our investment process begins with data pre-processing and normalization. We evaluate all the data that is used in our models for timeliness, quality and consistency. We then perform a number of market data normalizations that allow us to interpret and use the data consistently across asset classes. Unifi uses this data to power instrument-level asset pricing models that allow us to estimate the risk and return of every asset we review in our investment universe. We choose and calibrate our asset models to reflect real world market dynamics, economically meaningful parameters and robust quantitative fundamentals. 
 
Our asset models allow Unifi traders to flexibly and rapidly evaluate paired investment opportunities across markets in real time. We use market dashboards we have developed using our proprietary software to visualize inter- and intra-market pricing discrepancies, allowing traders to quickly identify and act on investment opportunities we believe provide high risk-adjusted returns. Unifi's portfolio objective is to construct a market-neutral portfolio through trade pairs with offsetting risk exposures, maximizing the potential for excess returns while minimizing portfolio risk. 
 
We have an acute focus on execution quality, which we feel is uniquely important in markets such as credit derivatives where liquidity can be scarce. To that end, our choice of investment strategies is highly responsive to market conditions, transaction costs and liquidity. At any given time, we expect to be looking for opportunistic entry points into 5-10 larger positions, even as we remain flexible and responsive across markets. 
 
The Unifi portfolio is actively managed in an effort to have no directional market exposure, limited left-tail drawdown risk and acceptable secondary exposures to convexity, jump to default and other risk factors.

results.strategy_description:
Pictet Asia Special Sits is a Pan-Asian Equity focused Event-Driven and special situations strategy. The strategy seeks to take advantage of the growth in corporate activity across the Asian continent focusing on less covered areas of the market. 
The strategy will be agnostic to the overall market direction and will aim to isolate the alpha of situations in the most efficient way including using derivatives. 
The strategy will target a wide range of corporate events which can be categorized in three types of opportunities: Defined Catalyst (ECM trades, dual listings, thematic baskets, Special Sits), Announced M&A and Pre-Event. The strategy will mix a deep fundamental analysis of companies and situations with a quantitative approach to portfolio construction, hedging and sizing.
 We aim to have a liquid and diversified book by sector, country and maturity profile of situations. The portfolio will typically contain between 25-40 situations. 
The strategy will have a bias towards protecting capital in down markets via a disciplined approach to risk management using both qualitative and quantitative assessments. Stop-losses will be determined for each situation. All currency risk will be fully hedged. 

The aim of the strategy will be to focus on delivering consistent uncorrelated returns with limited volatility throughout a cycle.

results.strategy_description:
The strategy’s investment objective is to achieve long-term capital appreciation while providing a degree of downside protection. To achieve this, we employ a long/short equity approach aiming to benefit from structural winners and losers in our investment universe. The fund invests primarily in the Greater China region (China, Hong Kong and Taiwan) whereby China accounts for the majority of exposure.

For long positions, we seek stocks with rising earnings forecast and low valuations. We call these stocks “Rising Stars.” In our view, typically such companies are subject to multiple expansion following positive earnings revisions. We hold a total of 50-80 long positions. Shorts comprise of companies with what we believe to be declining earnings momentum and hefty valuations. From our experiences, earnings disappointment is often followed by price declines. We call these “Fallen Angels.” We typically hold up to 40 short positions. Equally important is what we don’t do and that is companies where we believe the franchise is fully priced in or cheap companies with falling earnings, where negative news results in further price depreciation.

Gross exposure is between 60% and 200% while net exposure is typically between 20% and 80%.

results.strategy_description:
BDAF seeks to generate absolute returns with low volatility and low correlations to traditional asset classes through all market conditions, while maintaining target portfolio level net exposure within (+/- 10%). Capital is deployed based on perceived portfolio manager edge, background, strategy, volatility and correlations to the market and to other strategies. Live aggregated data allows for Boothbay to dynamically allocate capital and manage risk, at both the manager and overall fund level. 

BDAF believes in combining, what we believe are, non-correlated positive expectancy strategies into a cohesive portfolio, which we believe is further enhanced by operational and structural alphas. The fund attempts to optimize manager selection, allocation size, and concentrations through the use of its proprietary portfolio tool. The selection process involves customized terms and risk parameters for every strategy, and live, daily position-level transparency enables market neutral stance.

BDAF targets 1.25x vol to BBARS by being concentrated with less PMs overall compared to BDAF. BDAF does not allocate via first loss unlike BBARS and will have more exposure to FIRV and event-driven strategies.

The genesis of our equities’ investment philosophy consists of finding long-term value creation stories in Latin America, combined with rigorous risk management. The fund’s goal is to find medium to long-term opportunities in stocks with a set of pillars we view as necessary for an Equity story to prove profitable over the long run. The pillars we value include: (i) favorable sector trends; (ii) proven capital structure discipline and aligned interest to its minority shareholders; (iii) proper Environmental, Social, and Governance standards; and (iv) adequate valuation.
